newsitem.title: USA: U.S. Plains fed cattle market quiet, bid $68-trade.
newsitem.headline: U.S. Plains fed cattle market quiet, bid $68-trade.

text.p: U.S. Plains feedlot cattle markets early Tuesday were inactive, with no sales reported, feedlot sources said.
A few packer bids at $68.00 per cwt, steady with light sales Monday, were passed by cattle owners who were asking $69.00 to $70.00.
"A bid at $69.00 would buy a whole lot of cattle," one Kansas feedlot operator said.
Cattle owners appeared content to wait for higher bids amid ideas that packers would show increased demand by Wednesday, sources said.
Light sales on Monday spurred talk that several packers appeared to be short on supplies of slaughter-ready cattle, market sources said.
About 5,000 head traded in Kansas on Monday at $68.00, steady with last week's top price.
Beef movement Monday was "good" for a Monday, although packers discounted prices to move the beef, sources said.

Beef prices Monday were quoted down $0.80 to $0.92 per cwt for choice-grade beef at $114.14 to $116.69 and down $0.01 to $0.09 for select-grade at $95.68 to $97.68, USDA said. There were 155 loads of fabricated beef sold.
